problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}={e}^{2x}+{x}^{2}y,\,y(0)=1
$$

The trapezoidal method is applied with step size $Δx=2.$ Find the general formula for the new $y$ value, ${y}_{\text{new}},$ in terms of the current values $x$ and $y,$ and the new value ${x}_{\text{new}}.$
worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c,
$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy=\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

In this example, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}({e}^{2x}+{x}^{2}y+({e}^{2{x}_{\text{new}}}+{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}{y}_{\text{new}}))\cdot 2 \\  & ={e}^{2x}+{e}^{2{x}_{\text{new}}}+{x}^{2}y+{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}{y}_{\text{new}}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+{e}^{2x}+{e}^{2{x}_{\text{new}}}+{x}^{2}y+{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}{y}_{\text{new}} \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & ={e}^{2x}+{e}^{2{x}_{\text{new}}}+({x}^{2}+1)y+{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}{y}_{\text{new}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for the general formula for ${y}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}}-{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}{y}_{\text{new}} & ={e}^{2x}+{e}^{2{x}_{\text{new}}}+({x}^{2}+1)y \\ {y}_{\text{new}}(1-{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}) & ={e}^{2x}+{e}^{2{x}_{\text{new}}}+({x}^{2}+1)y \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{{e}^{2x}+{e}^{2{x}_{\text{new}}}+({x}^{2}+1)y}{1-{x}_{\text{new}}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$
